stall_points.quote: gate 6 (fix cap): {iterations} fix commit(s) on {branch} since {merge_base[:12]}, required at most {cap}. The cap is combined across ci/blueprint/review fixes (DESIGN.md:70-72); a PR past it needs human attention, not another merge attempt.
stall_points.trigger: check_fix_gates counts commits in merge_base..head whose subject starts with '[codex-auto-fix]' or '[codex-review-fix]'; if that count > MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP (default DEFAULT_FIX_CAP = 5) the merge is refused, regardless of CI/review being fully green. Exactly the PR #5 case: 6 > 5.
stall_points.rationale: The gate has two jobs conflated into one. The legitimate one is 'do not merge while the fix loop is thrashing' — and that is already covered by the live-lock probe immediately above (lines 212-222) and by gates 3/4 (CI green + clean verdict on this exact SHA). The count-based half fires on a PR whose loop has finished and whose evidence is green, and the message ('needs human attention, not another merge attempt') tells the operator the remedy is a human, not a decision it may take. Nothing in the code makes MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP owner-only: it is a plain os.environ.get with no provenance check, so the operator could have set it itself. It stopped because the GateFailure text says the situation belongs to a human, reinforced by goal.md's 'never weaken a gate to pass it'. A high fix count is a signal about review quality, not evidence the merge is unsafe.
stall_points.minimal_fix: Keep the count, drop the halt-on-count. Either (a) demote the over-cap case to a stderr warning plus a telemetry event when gates 3, 4 and 5 are all green and the fix lock is idle (the loop is provably finished), or (b) at minimum reword to name the operator's own remedy, e.g. '... the operator may re-run with MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP=<n> once CI and review are green on this head; record the reason in results/telemetry/events.md' — the same self-serve override phrasing dispatch.sh:364-366 already uses for --skip-hook-check.

stall_points.quote: FIX_COMMIT_PREFIXES = ("[codex-auto-fix]", "[codex-review-fix]")  ...  iterations = sum(1 for line in lines if not line.startswith("commit ") and line.startswith(FIX_COMMIT_PREFIXES))
stall_points.trigger: Any commit on the branch whose subject starts with one of the two prefixes counts against the cap — including commits the operator (or an agent.sh session) authored by hand while following the fix-commit naming convention. On PR #5 all six [codex-review-fix] commits are authored 'Dengnifer <ruixuan.deng@icloud.com>', not the bot identity autofix.sh uses (BOT_NAME/BOT_EMAIL, autofix.sh:71-72), and none carry autofix.sh's 'Iteration: N of 5 (combined cap)' trailer. autofix.sh's own counter never reached the cap and no '## Human attention required' note was ever posted.
stall_points.rationale: This is the actual mechanism behind today's interruption, and it is an over-generalization. The cap exists to bound the AUTOMATED fix loop (autofix.sh's ping-pong guard). pr_merge.py re-derives the count from subject prefixes alone, so an operator that repairs review findings itself and labels the commits with the house prefix mints its own gate-6 blocker — a self-inflicted stall with no runaway-loop behind it. The two counters also disagree structurally: autofix.sh counts against merge-base($BASE, local tip) with a local branch ref, pr_merge.py against merge-base(github/$base, head), so they can diverge on a branch that has merged the base in (PR #5 has exactly such a merge, eaa6b6e).
stall_points.minimal_fix: Count only commits autofix.sh actually made: require the bot author (MIPSTARRE_BOT_EMAIL / 'codex-bot@localhost') or the machine-generated trailer, e.g. `git rev-list --format='%s%x00%ae'` and count a commit only when the subject has a fix prefix AND the author email is the bot's. Operator-authored repairs then stop consuming the automated loop's budget.

stall_points.quote:
printf '## Human attention required

'  ...  printf '`%s..HEAD` — so the cap stays reached until a human takes over.

' "$BASE"  ...  printf 'Read the fix commits, the `local-ci/*` statuses on that SHA, and the review verdict for it before re-enabling.'
stall_points.trigger: run_phase is entered with FIX_ITERATIONS >= FIX_CAP (autofix.sh:695-696). The loop stops, this note is posted to the PR as an idempotent comment, a terminal forced review runs, and the script exits 0.
stall_points.rationale: Stopping the automated loop at the cap is deliberate and correct (it is the runaway-bot guard ported from auto-fix.yml). What is not justified is the escalation TARGET: the note names 'a human' as the only party who can take over and 're-enable'. The operator is the party that reads this note, and adjudication of remaining findings is explicitly its prerogative elsewhere (pr_merge.py:189 'past the round cap the operator may adjudicate what is left'; review.md §12). This wording is the upstream source of the belief that a capped PR is owner territory, and pr_merge.py:240 then repeats it at the merge gate.
stall_points.minimal_fix: Keep the loop stop; retarget the note. Replace the heading and the 'until a human takes over' sentence with the operator's actual options: adjudicate the remaining findings per review.md §12 and merge with --adjudicated, or raise MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP for one further round with an events.md entry. Escalate to the owner only for the cases goal.md lists (credentials, scope budget, unresolvable mathematics).

stall_points.quote:
if [ "$FIX_ITERATIONS" -ge "$FIX_CAP" ]; then
    cap_reached
  fi   ||   cap = int(os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP", DEFAULT_FIX_CAP))
    if iterations > cap:
stall_points.trigger: autofix.sh refuses to make fix commit number cap+1 (>=), so its own loop tops out at exactly 5 commits; pr_merge.py refuses only above cap (>). The two constants are the same env var but the comparisons differ, and the defaults are duplicated in two places (autofix.sh:60 'FIX_CAP="${MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP:-5}"' and pr_merge.py:53 'DEFAULT_FIX_CAP = 5').
stall_points.rationale: Not itself an owner stall, but it is why a cap-6 state is even reachable while the loop reports itself as never having capped: a branch at 6 prefixed commits cannot have been produced by autofix.sh alone, so the merge gate refuses on a condition the fix loop never signalled and never documented on the PR. An operator reading gate 6 has no cap-reached note to reconcile it against, which makes the refusal look like a rule it does not understand — the classic reason to escalate.
stall_points.minimal_fix: Make the boundaries agree and state them once: have pr_merge.py import the cap and the comparison semantics from a single place (or comment both call sites), and make gate 6 report whether autofix.sh's cap-reached marker is present on the PR, so a count that exceeds the cap without that marker is reported as 'these fix commits were not made by the fix loop' rather than as a loop overrun.

stall_points.trigger: Unresolved review findings exist on the head SHA but the PR carries no 'auto-fix-codex' label (MIPSTARRE_AUTO_FIX_LABEL). REVIEW_FIX stays 0, the review-fix phase is skipped, and autofix exits 0 'nothing to fix'. PR #5 currently carries no labels at all.
stall_points.rationale: The opt-in itself is deliberate (the auto-fix-claude analogue), but 'add the label on GitHub' reads as an out-of-band human action, and the lane gives the operator no obvious way to do it: gh_common.py exposes list-labels only — there is no add-label verb — and the sole label-writing path is pr_open.py --label, which also pushes the branch as a side effect (pr_open.py:145-147). The practical consequence on PR #5 is that the operator did all six review repairs by hand, which is exactly what tripped gate 6.
stall_points.minimal_fix: Keep the opt-in; close the capability gap. Add a small 'add-label' verb to gh_common.py (POST issues/<n>/labels, mutation+idempotent — the code already exists inline in pr_open.py:145-147) and change the log line to name it: 'enable with local/bin/gh_common.py add-label <PR> auto-fix-codex'.

entries.append((

The operator can in fact resolve it — re-run review.sh, or tick the box with a reason per pr_merge.py:187-188 — but the text names no machine-executable route, and autofix.sh cannot fix it either (the finding has no location). It is a stall manufactured by output formatting, not by any defect in the change.

stall_points.trigger: After a successful merge, local base has commits github/base does not (diverged). fast_forward_base returns False, and post_merge then skips the origin alias refresh, the cache warmer AND the branch/worktree cleanup, printing 'resolve local {base} first, then rerun them by hand'.

Declaring divergence 'a human's call' means the operator stops here rather than inspecting whether the local-only commits are its own (they usually are — telemetry commits).
stall_points.minimal_fix: Keep refusing the automatic fast-forward, but say what the operator may do and re-check: report the diverging commits (git log --oneline remote..base) and point at the operator-executable resolution, and let the alias refresh proceed when local base is merely behind or equal — only skip it when the two truly diverge.

But the suggested route, agent.sh, is guarded as 'human-invoked only' (agent.sh:205-215), so the operator reading this line is pointed at a tool that announces itself as not for automation. Whether it actually refuses depends on whether MIPSTARRE_AUTOMATION/MIPSTARRE_AUTOFIX_ACTIVE happen to be set in the operator's environment — an accidental, environment-dependent stall.

  # ------------------------------------------------------------- iteration cap
  # The bot-fix-guard analogue: ONE counter combined across ci, blueprint and
  # review fixes.  At the cap the loop stops, a human-attention note goes on the
  # PR, and the final bot-fix result gets its single forced review
  # (pr-review.yml:69-72 — "we only want to review human-authored pushes and the
  # final bot-fix result, detected by iteration cap").
  cap_reached() {
    local marker="<!-- autofix:cap-reached pr=$PR_NUM -->" note="$RUN_DIR/cap-note.md"
    log "combined fix-iteration cap reached ($FIX_ITERATIONS/$FIX_CAP) for PR $PR_NUM"
    {
      printf '## Human attention required\n\n'
      printf 'The combined auto-fix iteration cap (%s) was reached at %s on head `%s`.\n\n' "$FIX_CAP" "$(now_utc)" "$HEAD_SHA"
      printf 'No further automated fix runs on this branch.  The counter is the\n'
      printf 'branch history itself — the `%s` / `%s` commits in\n' "$PREFIX_AUTO" "$PREFIX_REVIEW"
      printf '`%s..HEAD` — so the cap stays reached until a human takes over.\n\n' "$BASE"
      printf 'Read the fix commits, the `local-ci/*` statuses on that SHA, and the\n'
      printf 'review verdict for it before re-enabling.  Repeated cap hits are\n'
      printf 'protocol evidence — record them in `results/telemetry/events.md`.\n'
    } >"$note"
  ...then: ensure-pr-comment (idempotent by marker), release_fix_lock FIRST (review.sh refuses a branch whose fix lock has a live holder), three push attempts, then ci.sh + review.sh --force-review, then exit 0.

verdicts.argument:
I attacked the "deleting the count loses nothing" claim eight ways; every attack failed against file:line evidence, and one attack failed so badly it inverts into positive support for deletion.

A. "A [codex-*-fix] commit can land after the review without invalidating it." FAILS. Gate 4 requires a review whose `commit_id == head_sha` AND whose body carries `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` (pr_merge.py:171-176); `gh_common.post_review` only ever creates a review with `commit_id` set to the reviewed SHA and never PATCHes a body across SHAs (gh_common.py:242-260). Gate 2 requires the local branch tip to equal the head SHA (pr_merge.py:139-143), gate 2b re-fetches and requires the head to contain the live base tip (pr_merge.py:~300-312), and `merge_pr` merges through the REST `sha` guard with a merged read-back (gh_common.py:277-290). review.sh additionally re-checks `head_moved` and publishes NOTHING if the head moved while the reviewer was thinking (review.sh:~1010-1016).

B. "CI statuses on the head can be stale or forged." FAILS. ci.sh refuses to publish unless the worktree HEAD is exactly the GitHub head (ci.sh:763), publishes nothing at all for partial `--only/--skip-build/--base` runs (ci.sh:527-535, 761), dies on a dirty worktree before publishing (ci.sh:764-767) and withholds `local-ci/summary` if the tree became dirty mid-run (ci.sh:1229-1233). `skipped -> success` (ci.sh:1178) is derived from a real `merge-base..head` diff (ci.sh:586, 601, 1028), and statuses are per-SHA, with autofix stamping `pending` on every new SHA (autofix.sh:781-786).

C. "The bot-commit skip lets an unreviewed fix commit merge." This is the one real hole in the ladder (review.sh:428-435 exits 0 without publishing when the head subject is bot-prefixed) — but it fails CLOSED at gate 4, not at gate 6: no review on the head means refusal (pr_merge.py:171-176). The count is not what protects it.

D. "Hand-ticked or carried-over findings fake a clean ledger." FAILS. Findings never cross SHAs (review.md:270-283), `preserve_prior` deliberately does not merge ledgers (review.sh:633-637), and gate 4 demands BOTH a clean ledger and `local-review/summary == success`, which review.sh computes from the same run (review.sh:1030-1043, pr_merge.py:180-186).

E. "Autofix races pr_merge." FAILS — gate 6(a) is kept (pr_merge.py:212-222) and the REST sha guard is atomic.

F. "The cap is an independent second opinion on the loop." FAILS, decisively and in reverse: autofix.sh:60 and pr_merge.py:236 read the SAME `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP`. Raising it raises both at once, so gate 6(b) never was an independent bound on anything.

G. Coverage: the review that greenlights the head diffs the FULL `MERGE_BASE..HEAD_SHA` range (review.sh:489-494), so every fix commit's content is inside the approving review no matter how many there were. The count adds no content-coverage property.

H. Reachability. With a constant cap, autofix cannot produce more than FIX_CAP fix commits: the count is re-derived from branch history at startup (autofix.sh:401-408) and re-checked before EVERY phase (autofix.sh:695-696). So gate 6(b) can only ever fire on commits the fix loop did not make — and PR #5 proves exactly that. All six `[codex-review-fix]` commits on `issue-0006-qpbt-minimal-skeleton` (b5da371, 99ccb0c, f36df43, 0aacbca, 3b394f2, 356ec27) are authored AND committed by `Dengnifer <ruixuan.deng@icloud.com>` with no `Machine-generated by local/bin/autofix.sh` trailer; autofix's own commits are made as `codex[bot]` (autofix.sh:73-74, 770-775). autofix.sh never ran on this branch; its cap never fired. Gate 6(b) is measuring an operator-driven repair that borrowed the bot subject prefix, not a runaway fix loop.

Live evidence on head b5da371de32d: all eight `local-ci/<step>` plus `local-ci/summary` are `success`, `local-review/summary` is `success`, and the marker-bound COMMENT review on that exact commit id reads `VERDICT: APPROVED (code=APPROVED, prose=n/a)` with 0 unchecked findings. Gate 6(b) is the only refusal, and its message ("needs human attention, not another merge attempt") is a pure owner-stall.

What IS genuinely lost is not safety but observability: autofix.md:181-184 calls a cap hit "protocol evidence" for telemetry, and after deletion nothing at merge time flags an operator-driven review->fix->review cascade (each round of which, in PR #5, needed `review.sh --force-review` to get past review.sh:428-435 — four such forced reviews exist on this PR, against review.md:145-149 which reserves `--force-review` for the single terminal review at the cap). That is a cost/termination and record-keeping concern, not a soundness one: an unbounded cascade never merges anything unsound, it only burns time, and review.md §12's round cap plus `--adjudicated` (pr_merge.py:188-203) already handles non-convergence without the owner.
verdicts.amendments:
Three amendments; the first is mandatory or the change introduces a real correctness regression.

1. MANDATORY — do not delete the merge-base computation with the count. `check_fix_gates` returns `merge_base` (pr_merge.py:244) and gate 7 uses it to scan commit messages for GitHub's closing keywords: `git log --format=%B merge_base..head` (pr_merge.py:250-252, 256-262). Deleting "(b) entirely" as phrased would take out the base-ref resolution loop (pr_merge.py:224-233) and the `merge-base` call (pr_merge.py:234). That `git log` runs with `check=False`, so a broken range returns "" SILENTLY and gate 7 degrades to scanning the PR body only — a PR that closes an issue via a commit-message keyword, where that issue still has open sub-issues, would then merge. Delete only pr_merge.py:235-241 (the `rev-list`, the `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` read, the `iterations > cap` refusal). Keep 224-234 verbatim, including the fail-closed `GateFailure` when no base ref resolves, and relabel it from "gate 6 (fix cap)" to something like "gate 7 (base ref)" so the message names the gate it actually serves. Adjust the `passed(...)` line at 242 to report only the lock result.

2. RECOMMENDED — keep the count as a printed warning, not a refusal. One `sys.stderr.write` line ("N fix-prefixed commits since <merge base>; autofix's own cap is M") preserves the telemetry signal autofix.md:181-184 asks for, and keeps the anomaly visible in `--check-only` output, at zero stall cost.
